Columbus browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal Columbus TDR-5 Tube Driver Published on November 30, 2005 Columbus overdrive pedal Information The Columbus TDR-5 Tube Driver is a Japanese-made overdrive and distortion pedal produced in the late 1980s and early 1990s. It shares identical circuitry with the Axtron, Profile+, Series 10, and Vision TDR-5 models, differing only in branding. Manufactured by Aria or a related Japanese OEM, this pedal is part of a compact plastic-cased series typical of the period. Despite its name, it does not contain a vacuum tube. Instead, it uses an analog solid-state circuit built around discrete transistor stages, typically employing 2SC1815 (C1815) transistors similar to those used in contemporary Maxon and Ibanez designs. The circuit delivers a versatile drive range, covering smooth, mid-focused overdrive and more saturated distortion textures. Its tonal response is shaped by a two-band EQ section offering separate High and Low controls, a feature uncommon in compact pedals of its time. These controls allow significant tonal adjustment, letting the pedal adapt well to different amplifiers and pickup types. The pedal's voicing has often been described as sitting between a Tube Screamer-style midrange push and the sharper tone of late-80s Japanese distortions. The Columbus TDR-5 includes buffered bypass for consistent signal integrity and operates on standard 9V DC power or battery. The enclosure, molded from sturdy plastic, reflects the design conventions of late-1980s Japanese OEM pedals. Its sonic character and uncommon dual EQ layout have made it a sought-after piece among collectors and enthusiasts of vintage Japanese effects. Controls Level: Adjusts the overall output volume. Drive: Sets the amount of gain and distortion. High: Boosts or cuts high frequencies. Low: Boosts or cuts low frequencies. Connections Input: Standard 1/4" mono instrument input. Output: Standard 1/4" mono output. Power: 9V DC input jack or 9V battery compartment.
